title: White Rice with Tomatoes and/or Tomato‑Based Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: White rice is a polished grain product from which the husk and bran have been removed. In this version the rice is served with tomatoes and/or a tomato‑based sauce, adding bright flavor and a boost of vitamins and antioxidants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice is a staple food for more than half of the world’s population.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Tomato sauce is often made from ripe tomatoes, olive oil, and herbs, enhancing nutrient absorption.
White rice digests quickly, making it a common choice for recovery diets.
The rice‑and‑tomato combination is traditional in Mediterranean and Asian cuisines.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides complex carbohydrates, the body’s primary fuel for daily activities.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Tomatoes add dietary fiber and digestive enzymes that promote healthy gut function.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: May reduce cardiovascular risk
items.content: The blend of complex carbs from rice and potassium from tomatoes can help maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or tomato products.

items.title: Sodium in sauce
items.content: Prepared tomato sauce often contains added salt; choose low‑sodium versions when possible.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Tomatoes may be treated with pesticides; opting for organic or well‑washed produce reduces exposure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice with tomatoes hot as a side dish or a main course. It pairs well with vegetables, meat, fresh herbs, a drizzle of olive oil, or a squeeze of lemon to brighten the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice with tomato sauce should be cooled promptly and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days.
